Definition: from a presumed compound of G2556 and G2192; to maltreat:--which suffer adversity, torment.
BiblicalUsage: Kakoucheo is to maltreat — to suffer hardship with those who suffer. The heroes of faith were destitute, afflicted, tormented; and the Hebrews are told to remember them that are in bonds, as bound with them, and them which suffer adversity, as being yourselves also in the body.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word makes suffering a shared thing: I am to remember the afflicted as if I were bound with them, because in the body of Christ their bonds are mine too.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
